record.title: Smith.ai pricing: AI calls, human service and Revo
record.description: Review Smith.ai pricing, billing units and buying questions for home service teams. Compare the workflow with Revo’s current plans.
record.lead: Choose the service model before comparing the call allowance.
record.intro: Smith.ai offers separate AI and human receptionist products. A contractor evaluating its pricing needs to identify who will answer, which tasks require a person and how repeat calls affect the monthly allowance. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: The AI Free plan lists 25 calls for $0 monthly, then $3 per extra call. The baseline Pro option is $150 for 75 calls, with $2.50 extra calls; baseline Enterprise is $500 for 300, with $2.17 extras. These are call allowances, not minute bundles. AI scheduling is listed; confirm your calendar and live-escalation terms.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: For a remodeling company, a long project inquiry and a short appointment change can each use a call. That makes call count useful, but it does not tell you whether the caller received the right answer. Keep new estimates, existing projects and supplier calls separate when testing. If a human must handle a particular request, confirm the handoff and its billing before selecting the AI tier.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: Illustrative arithmetic: 100 billable calls on baseline AI Pro cost $212.50 before other applicable charges: $150 plus 25 extra calls at $2.50. This is a workload example, not a quote or a forecast. Do not apply this AI calculation to the separately priced human receptionist service.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Obtain separate AI-first and human-first proposals if both are under consideration.
Ask what counts as a real call and how spam exclusions are applied.
Test an estimate request, a calendar change and an escalation to a person.
Check cancellation notice and any longer-term offer separately.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Does Smith.ai charge for minutes?
faqs.a: The AI table reviewed here uses calls. Request the exact billing definition for the product and package you choose.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: Choose the service model before comparing the call allowance. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.

record.title: Davinci Virtual pricing: business hours or Premium
record.description: Review Davinci Virtual pricing, billing units and buying questions for home service teams. Compare the workflow with Revo’s current plans.
record.lead: Match the live coverage window and appointment tier to your office.
record.intro: This guide concerns Davinci Virtual live receptionists, not unrelated products named Davinci. For a home-service business, both the live answering hours and the tier needed for appointments affect the comparison. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: Business 50 is $129 monthly and Business 100 is $239; Premium 50 is $249 and Premium 100 is $319. The FAQ lists $95 setup and extra minutes at $1.75 for Business or $2.50 for Premium. Live answering is Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–8 p.m. Eastern; around-the-clock automation is different coverage. Appointment scheduling is listed under Premium.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: A home inspector taking daytime estimate inquiries may have different needs from a plumbing company receiving overnight calls. Translate Eastern hours into your operating timezone and include weekends in the review. If booking is required, compare the Premium package rather than assuming the Business entry price provides the same workflow.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: For an illustrative western-US office, write out when the live receptionist window overlaps the workday and when automation takes over. Test the handoff at the boundary with an appointment change and an urgent request. Specify what the caller should hear after hours; neither automation nor message capture establishes that a technician is available.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Confirm the time zone and holiday coverage.
Price Premium when direct appointment work is required.
Include setup and the correct tier’s extra-minute rate.
Document the after-hours follow-up expectation.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Does 24/7 automation mean 24/7 live receptionists?
faqs.a: No. The reviewed offer distinguishes its weekday live-answering window from automated coverage outside that window.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: Match the live coverage window and appointment tier to your office. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.

record.title: MAP Communications pricing: PAYG versus minute plans
record.description: Review MAP Communications pricing, billing units and buying questions for home service teams. Compare the workflow with Revo’s current plans.
record.lead: Compare seasonal workload against the full usage calculation.
record.intro: MAP Communications publishes pay-as-you-go and bundled live-answering prices. A contractor can compare these using billed minutes, while keeping feature scope and any extra fees explicit. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: PAYG lists $49 monthly, no included minutes and $1.37 per minute. Business is $179 for 125 minutes with $1.30 extras; Enterprise is $339 for 250 with $1.28; Premium is $649 for 500 with $1.28. The page lists 24/7 coverage, English/Spanish service and no long-term contracts.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: A tree-service office may have quiet months followed by a burst of inquiries. Compare the same routing policy in both periods: sending every call versus forwarding only when the office is busy creates different workloads. Do not assume a named field-service connection exists without verifying it for the chosen setup.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: Illustrative usage of 100 billed minutes is $186 on PAYG before unverified extras: $49 plus 100 × $1.37. Business has a $179 base covering up to 125 minutes, so its base is lower at that workload. Repeat the calculation for your actual quiet and busy periods, including any proposal-specific tasks or fees.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Ask for the billed-minute definition and rounding.
Compare an ordinary month with the seasonal peak.
Verify how language choice and transfers are configured.
Confirm any software connection rather than inferring it from answering coverage.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Is PAYG always the cheapest option for low volume?
faqs.a: Use the actual usage calculation. At some minute levels a bundle’s base can be lower; the crossover also depends on any additional quoted fees.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: Compare seasonal workload against the full usage calculation. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.

record.title: ReceptionHQ pricing: messages, calls and appointments
record.description: Review ReceptionHQ pricing, billing units and buying questions for home service teams. Compare the workflow with Revo’s current plans.
record.lead: A message-taking fee is not a complete appointment-handling quote.
record.intro: ReceptionHQ’s US product range separates message taking from broader receptionist and appointment tasks. Start with what the office needs completed, then compare the relevant service’s call unit. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: MessageExpress starts at $25 monthly plus $1.99 per call on PAYG. ReceptionistPlus starts at $35; MyAssistant and MyDiary start at $49 each. MyDiary addresses appointment handling. These starting figures are not all-inclusive bills. Additional or after-hours charges require plan-level confirmation; broader availability does not mean every overnight call is US-staffed.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: A window-cleaning office that only wants a callback name and number can evaluate a narrower service than a team needing appointments handled. Define the minimum useful message and whether the caller needs to choose a slot. Compare US pricing and coverage, rather than applying another country’s similar product name or rate.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: For an illustrative message-only month with 20 billable PAYG calls, the stated MessageExpress base and call charges give $64.80 before any other charges: $25 plus 20 × $1.99. That example does not establish the cost of booking appointments. Request a separate MyDiary scope and quote if that is the required outcome.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Choose message taking, receptionist support or appointment handling explicitly.
Confirm what counts as a billable call.
Ask for after-hours and transfer charges.
Check US service coverage and the exact appointment permissions.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Does the $25 starting price establish a booking-service bill?
faqs.a: No. It refers to the reviewed MessageExpress starting option with additional per-call charges. Appointment handling belongs to a different scope.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: A message-taking fee is not a complete appointment-handling quote. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.

record.title: GoTo AI Receptionist pricing: credits and phone seats
record.description: Review GoTo AI Receptionist pricing, billing units and buying questions for home service teams. Compare the workflow with Revo’s current plans.
record.lead: Request a quote that explains the AIR credit unit.
record.intro: GoTo’s current Connect pricing organizes AI Receptionist alongside its phone-system packages. Without a published dollar rate and credit conversion, an invented per-minute calculation would obscure the purchase decision. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: The current plan page lists Phone System + AI Receptionist and CX Complete, with 100 AIR credits and additional credits available. Pricing requires sales contact. No dollar total or credit-to-minute conversion was verified. An April 2025 FAQ describes different minute packages, so it should not be used as the current price card.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: An office replacing several phone seats should budget the phone platform and AI usage together. An existing GoTo customer should ask for the incremental change to the current subscription. Define the routing and languages the business needs in the proposal; a historical English-only FAQ and a current multilingual card should not be merged into one undated specification.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: Give the provider an illustrative week of calls, including short questions, longer estimate inquiries and transfers. Ask it to show the AIR-credit debit for each example and the total phone-seat bill. Keep the estimate blank until the unit conversion is documented. A credit allowance without its consumption rule is not enough to compare a busy month.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Request phone seats, numbers and AIR charges on separate lines.
Obtain the credit consumption and extra-credit rates.
Confirm the current language and routing scope.
Check which product generation the proposal describes.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Can I turn 100 AIR credits into 100 minutes?
faqs.a: No verified conversion supports that assumption. Ask GoTo to document the consumption rule before estimating usage.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: Request a quote that explains the AIR credit unit. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.

record.title: Zoom AI Receptionist pricing: standalone versus Phone
record.description: Review Zoom AI Receptionist pricing, billing units and buying questions for home service teams. Compare the workflow with Revo’s current plans.
record.lead: Identify the offer before using a published Zoom price.
record.intro: Zoom Virtual Agent Receptionist, Zoom Phone AI answering and visitor reception in Zoom Rooms are different buying contexts. A service-business phone comparison must identify the specific product and purchase path. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: The July 9, 2026 standalone announcement states a starting price of $29.99 monthly for 100 minutes, or $24.99 monthly with annual billing. Other official pages describe included Zoom Phone AI answering or a per-minute add-on. These statements do not establish one universal current rate. Current overage, taxes and bundle applicability remain unverified here.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: A standalone office line and an existing Zoom Phone deployment should receive different proposals. Ask which licenses are required and whether the quoted allowance belongs to the standalone product or the phone bundle. Do not mistake a visitor kiosk for a customer-call answering service simply because both are called receptionist products.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: For an illustrative service office, prepare a standalone route and an existing-Zoom-Phone route. Use the same call mix, booking requirement and fallback number in both. Ask the provider to explain the applicable allowance and what happens above it. Keep extra-usage dollar totals unknown until the current terms resolve the purchase path.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Name the exact product and standalone or bundled offer.
Confirm monthly versus annual commitment.
Request the applicable allowance and excess-usage policy.
Test phone intake and handoff rather than a visitor-kiosk workflow.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Is one Zoom receptionist price valid for every purchase path?
faqs.a: No. The official statements reviewed describe different offers. Confirm the exact standalone or Zoom Phone arrangement before comparing totals.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: Identify the offer before using a published Zoom price. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.

record.title: OpenPhone AI pricing today: Quo Sona calls and base plan
record.description: Review Quo Sona pricing, billing units and buying questions for home service teams. Compare the workflow with Revo’s current plans.
record.lead: Add the required phone subscription to the Sona allowance.
record.intro: OpenPhone changed its name to Quo in September 2025. Buyers searching for the earlier AI receptionist should evaluate the current Sona offer on Quo, rather than treating the 2025 launch package as today’s price. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: Current Sona pricing lists 10 calls included on Quo plans. Paid tiers are $25 for 40 calls, $49 for 100, $99 for 250 and $199 for 600, with respective overages of $0.75, $0.65, $0.55 and $0.45 per call. Paid Quo service is required; Sona is not standalone. The underlying seat price must be verified before calculating a combined bill.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: A garage-door office using its phone system for both staff conversations and overflow answering needs to separate those activities. Decide which incoming calls reach Sona, which stay with the team and how repeated callers are counted. A message captured by the agent should not be treated as proof that a field-service appointment was created.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: Illustrative Sona-only usage of 120 billable calls on the $49/100-call tier is $62: $49 plus 20 × $0.65. The required Quo subscription and any other charges are additional. This is not a complete phone-system quote. Compare the full seat-and-agent proposal before changing an existing number or call flow.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Use current Quo/Sona terms instead of the old OpenPhone launch table.
Add the required base subscription to the estimate.
Confirm the billable-call definition and overflow routing.
Test what happens when the office takes back an AI-handled call.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Can I buy Sona as a standalone answering subscription?
faqs.a: The reviewed offer requires paid Quo service. Compare the combined phone and AI cost rather than the Sona add-on alone.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: Add the required phone subscription to the Sona allowance. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.
